original.description: Three-quarter-length portrait of Generalfeldmarschall Karl von Bülow in field-grey (M1910) service tunic with red piping, peaked cap, Pour le Mérite, Iron Cross and breast star; c. 1916, published in the Berliner Illustrirte Zeitung 12/1916.

original.licence: public domain — photographer died 1918 (life + 70); published before 1931

caption: Karl von Bülow (1846–1921), commander of the German 2nd Army — Liège, Namur, Charleroi, Guise; his call for Kluck to wheel inward and his decision to retreat from the Marne on 9 September, in consultation with Hentsch. Photographed c. 1916 as Generalfeldmarschall. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Rudolf Dührkoop, c. 1916, Berliner Illustrirte Zeitung; public domain (via Wikimedia Commons). Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Provided by Dave 2026-08-22. The only one of the German portraits in field-grey — useful contrast with Kluck's pre-war Dunkelblau on the uniforms & kit cards.
